stories.headline: Eurocontrol Revises 2026 European Traffic Forecast Downward
stories.lead: European flight volumes returned to 2019 levels in 2025, but the 2026 outlook has been adjusted following geopolitical escalations in the Middle East.
stories.source_description: In Europe, 2025 closed 4% above 2024 , reaching 100% of 2019 traffic levels with an average of 30,263 daily flights , returning to pre-pandemic volumes at 11.05 million flights. The October 2025 forecast proved to be slightly below the actual 2025 outturn, mainly due to stronger‑than‑expected traffic growth in southern and eastern Europe, as well as robust beyond‑ECAC flows. Traffic in the ECAC area is now expected to reach around 11.3 million flights for the year , corresponding to +2.7% growth compared with 2025 (±1.8pp) . This revision reflects increased geopolitical uncertainty, weaker demand assumptions, and operational disruptions, all of which are partly offset by still‑solid underlying traffic momentum. stories.headline: London Heathrow Retains Top Spot in OAG Megahubs 2025 Connectivity Rankings
stories.lead: London Heathrow retained its title as the world's most connected airport for the third consecutive year in the OAG Megahubs 2025 ranking. Meanwhile, Istanbul Airport and Frankfurt registered substantial connectivity gains, while Tokyo Haneda experienced a decline.
stories.source_description: London Heathrow (LHR) retains its title as the world’s most connected airport for the third consecutive year , offering over 59,000 possible connections to 226 destinations* on the busiest day**. Istanbul Airport (IST) has seen one of the greatest increases, surging from 8 th position last year to 2 nd place in this year’s ranking, due to a 25% year-on-year increase in potential connections on the busiest day of the year. Frankfurt (FRA) has seen a significant shift in rankings, climbing from 10 th position last year to 4 th , driven by a 21% increase in potential connections year-on-year. Tokyo Haneda (HND) has dropped down in this year’s rankings from 3 rd in 2024 to 9 th in 2025, reflecting a 10% decline in connections. Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson (ATL) – the world’s largest airport by seat capacity – re-enters the Top 10 this year rising from 11 th place last year to 8 th position in 2025. ATL has added eight (8) more destinations and seen a corresponding 14% increase in potential connections. Chicago O’Hare (ORD) also makes gains, climbing two (2) spots to 7th, due to a 17% growth in connections and an expanded network of 15 additional destinations.
detailed_analysis: London Heathrow (LHR) offers over 59,000 possible connections to 226 destinations on its busiest day to hold 1st place for the third consecutive year.

stories.headline: Emirates Launches Travel Rehearsal Program in Colombia
stories.lead: Emirates, an Autism-Certified Airline, hosted a Travel Rehearsal at El Dorado International Airport in Bogotá, Colombia, marking the first initiative of its kind in the country.
stories.source_description: Bogotá, Colombia, 16 October 2026: Emirates, the world’s first Autism-Certified Airline, hosted a Travel Rehearsal at El Dorado International Airport, the first initiative of its kind in Colombia. Delivered in line with Emirates’ commitment to Accessible Travel and El Dorado International Airport’s ‘El Dorado + Accessible’ programme, the Travel Rehearsal aims to make air travel more predictable, comfortable and accessible for individuals on the autism spectrum. The initiative enables travellers with accessible requirements to participate in a guided simulation of the complete air travel journey, helping them become familiar with airport procedures and onboard environments ahead of their trip. At El Dorado International Airport, individuals on the autism spectrum from local communities were invited to experience every stage of the airport journey, including check-in, baggage drop, security screening, and boarding. Participants also visited an Emirates aircraft, met cabin crew members, and completed a simulated arrival experience, including baggage reclaim and customs procedures. Gianmarco Mazetti, Emirates’ Area Manager, Colombia, said: “Being the world’s first Autism-Certified Airline, we take pride in advancing our commitment to making travel accessible for everyone. The Travel Rehearsal provided participants an opportunity to experience the airport journey in a relaxed and supportive environment, helping them build confidence and feel prepared for future travel. We would like to thank El Dorado International Airport for its support and for sharing our vision of empowering people across the spectrum to travel with ease. This activation would not have been possible without the Emirates Airport Services management and team, who helped organise and host the experience.” “El Dorado More Accessible is a set of programs designed to improve airport accessibility for passengers with non-visible disabilities. These include the Sunflower Program and ‘El Dorado at Your Own Pace’, an initiative that allows passengers who may experience travel-related anxiety to become familiar with the airport journey and procedures before their day of travel and making travel more accessible,” added Victor Alfredo Sanchez, Director of Customer Experience and Service at El Dorado International Airport . Emirates became the world’s first Autism-Certified Airline, with more than 35,000 cabin crew and ground staff completing specialised autism awareness training. The programme equips employees with in-depth knowledge of the autism spectrum, common misconceptions, challenges faced during travel, and personalised support strategies tailored to individual passenger needs. Since April 2025, Emirates’ Airport Services teams have come together to arrange more than 40 of these travel rehearsals for over 250 families across airports like Accra, Antananarivo, Athens, Bali, Bangalore, Barcelona, Bologna, Brussels, Cairo, Cebu, Christchurch, Da Nang, Delhi, Dubai, Dublin, Durban, Düsseldorf, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Guangzhou, Hanoi, Harare, Hong Kong, Istanbul, London, Luanda, Lusaka, Madrid, Male, Mauritius, Milan, Newcastle, Nice, Orlando, Oslo, Paris, Pampanga, Peshawar, Port Louis, Rome, Stansted, Stockholm, Sydney, Toronto, Trivandrum, Venice and Vienna.

stories.headline: Delta funding helps Clayton County nonprofit strengthen food delivery services
stories.lead: Delta Air Lines, through its Clayton County Donor Advised Fund, provided a $25,000 grant to The Online Food Pantry Mobile Food Market. This funding supports the nonprofit's efforts to restore food delivery services in six metro Atlanta counties after a critical delivery van was destroyed.
stories.source_description: A Clayton County nonprofit that delivers food directly to Georgia families in need is expanding its ability to serve the community, with support from Delta. Since its founding in 2018 by CEO Frederick West, The Online Food Pantry Mobile Food Market has helped more than 80,000 people access food assistance by recovering surplus food from local partners and delivering it to residents across six metro Atlanta counties. When the organization's delivery van, a critical part of its operation, was destroyed by fire earlier this year, the Delta Air Lines Clayton County Donor Advised Fund at the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provided a $25,000 grant to help purchase a replacement vehicle and restore delivery services. “Delta’s generous donation came at a critical moment for The Online Food Pantry," said West. "Their support didn't just help us replace a vehicle — it helped us restore hope, maintain our ability to serve our community, and continue making sure that food reaches those who need it most.” During a recent food delivery with West, it became clear that the new van also needed refrigeration to safely transport fresh produce, meat and other perishable items. To help meet that need, an additional $35,000 grant was awarded to install a refrigeration system and support operating expenses. “Since the Delta Air Lines Clayton County Charitable Fund was established last year, we've worked closely with Delta to help direct resources to organizations making a real difference in Clayton County,” said Daniel Lewis, philanthropic advisor at the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta. “This is a great example of that partnership in action.” Delta and The Delta Air Lines Foundation support 22 food banks in cities and regions across the globe to help fight hunger and food insecurity all year long, investing more than $1.8 million through corporate funding and grants in 2026 alone. About The Online Food Pantry Mobile Food Market The Online Food Pantry is a 501c3 nonprofit, established in early 2018 to eradicate food waste and combat hunger in communities with an online ordering platform and free home delivery service for anyone experiencing food insecurity. Volunteers pick up purchased food or rescue nutritious food from local food outlets. About the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta Since 1951, the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta has helped generations of Atlantans turn their love for the region into lasting change. The organization stewards more than $1.8 billion in assets and deploys more than $235 million annually to thousands of nonprofit partners; helps organizations across Atlanta meet immediate needs, sustain essential programs and respond to emerging challenges; and helps individuals, families, businesses and their advisors turn charitable goals into lasting impact through tax-smart giving options, personal guidance and local expertise.
